title: Saved computation, overwrites, and early exit
expectation: Data flow changes only under enabled && useSaved. The saved copy survives overwrites of current; override affects the surrounding computation but not the region of change.

title: Changed write killed by two layers of assignments
expectation: The change reaches no return branch: second selects 10 or 20. The comparison covers normal returns, not every possible effect of arithmetic evaluation.

title: Condition snapshot and a new version of a mutable guard
expectation: Before the change, decision equals !first; afterward, it equals second. Data flow changes under (!first && !second) || (first && second); original remains a snapshot of first.

title: Swapped operands through copies and repeated reads
expectation: Data flow changes in all four reverse/negate combinations: operand roles matter, not just the set of sources {a,b}. Repeated reads of delta must not mix write versions. The change does not prove unequal values for every input.

title: Short-circuiting and an executed unknown call
expectation: Under !enabled, the call is skipped and return data flow is unchanged. Under enabled, the result/completion remains unknown even under !chooseCaptured: the call has already executed. The numerical checks separately define mystery(x)=x*3; the CLI receives no such model.

title: Two conditional sources, early exit, and sign reversal
expectation: Under enabled, the selected right operand changes in every first/second/negate combination. Under !enabled, the return value 0 is unchanged. Sources may coincide within a computation after the change; their operand roles must still be preserved.

title: Nullish selection, a saved copy, and an independent return
expectation: The saved computation changes under useSaved, while !useSaved returns 100. For unrestricted inputs, falsy does not mean nullish: 0 must keep a selected, while null must select b. A conservative Unknown for unresolved selection is a precision limit, not evidence of no change.

title: Arithmetic reassociation with rounding and early return
expectation: The computation structure changes under !skip; under skip, the return value remains 0. Algebraic associativity does not prove equality for JS numbers: [1e16,-1e16,1,false,false] produces 2 -> 0. For [1,2,3,false,false], the values coincide even though data flow changed.

title: Loop accumulation and the zero-iteration branch
expectation: For positive finite integer count, the normal numerical result changes; count=0 returns 0. Loops are excluded from the initial function-result subset: the report must explicitly say Unknown/Unsupported rather than claim unchanged results or loop termination for all unrestricted inputs.

title: Change to an uncalled nested function that captures inputs
expectation: helper is never called; its returns and changed computation must not enter the result of outer. Data flow of outer is unchanged for every input with an established normal return; global source alignment may remain Partial because the file changed.
